Hey all!

While answering this MSE question I found something that surprised me. Write ⊗\otimes⊗ for Day convolution on the category of (N,+)(\mathbb{N},+)(N,+)-sets. Then unless I made a mistake somewhere, it seems like the following categories are all equivalent:

  • The category of cocommutative comonoids in N\mathbb{N}N-Set
  • The category of comonoids in N\mathbb{N}N-Set
  • The category of objects XXX in N\mathbb{N}N-Set with maps ϵ:X→N\epsilon : X \to \mathbb{N}ϵ:X→N and Δ:X→X⊗X\Delta : X \to X \otimes XΔ:X→X⊗X satisfying the counital laws
  • The category of ω\omegaω-chains of surjections of sets X0↠X1→X2↠⋯X_0 \twoheadrightarrow X_1 \to X_2 \twoheadrightarrow \cdotsX0​↠X1​→X2​↠⋯.

In particular, it seems like coassociativity and cocommutativity come for free, which I found very surprising... Is this a general feature of comonoids in M-sets? Maybe for some family of monoids? I'm curious if other people have run across this (or other things like it) before.
Also, rereading the original question, it seems natural to ask for which monoids MMM the category of (cocommutative?) comonoids in MMM-Set is again a topos.

Hi! Good to see you!

I believe there's a simple proof that in any cartesian category CCC each object becomes a comonoid in a unique way, namely via the diagonal. So it's automatically cocommutative. And the category of comonoids in CCC, or cocommutative monoids in CCC, is just CCC.

This is with the Day convolution product inherited from (N,+)(\mathbb{N}, {+})(N,+) treated as a discrete monoidal category though, not the Cartesian product, so that doesn't really apply. The question is confusing though because MMM-Set usually refers to presheaves on the delooping of MMM (MMM treated as a 1-object category), rather than presheaves on MMM treated as a discrete monoidal category.

Yeah, I probably shouldn't have said "Day convolution". I was trying to use a new word, haha. Explicitly I mean the tensor product of MMM-sets where X⊗YX \otimes YX⊗Y is X×Y/(m⋅x,y)∼(x,m⋅y)X \times Y \big / (m \cdot x, y) \sim (x, m \cdot y)X×Y/(m⋅x,y)∼(x,m⋅y).

(And of course by "MMM-sets" I mean "presheaves on MMM viewed as a one-object category")

Okay, so first, the action of the monoid MMM on any tensor product of two or more things factors through the abelianization of MMM because (m∘n)⋅(x,y)=m⋅n⋅(x,y)=m⋅(n⋅x,y)=(n⋅x,m⋅y)=n⋅(x,m⋅y)=n⋅m⋅(x,y)=(n∘m)⋅(x,y)(m \circ n) \cdot (x,y) = m \cdot n \cdot (x,y) = m \cdot (n \cdot x,y) = (n \cdot x, m \cdot y) = n \cdot (x, m \cdot y) = n \cdot m \cdot (x,y) = (n \circ m) \cdot (x,y)(m∘n)⋅(x,y)=m⋅n⋅(x,y)=m⋅(n⋅x,y)=(n⋅x,m⋅y)=n⋅(x,m⋅y)=n⋅m⋅(x,y)=(n∘m)⋅(x,y) ...

Hm... But actually, this is making me wonder a bunch of stuff about Day convolution (which I'm still pretty new to)... Like is there a way in which the discrete monoidal category attached to M relates to the one-object category BM? Also, since our M is commutative, doesn't BM become a monoidal category as well? Iirc a monoidal structure on BM is related to M being a monoid object in monoids? If that's right then M-sets should get a Day convolution product... Is that the same as the product I described earlier? It's just past midnight for me so I should go to bed, but there's a lot to think about here

(Also I guess I forgot to write that M was commutative when copying the problem here, but if you check the original MSE post that inspired this thread you'll see that was one of the assumptions. That might also be responsible for some of the confusion)
You can also deloop MMM as a discrete monoidal category to get a locally discrete bicategory BMBMBM so delooping and adding a trivial dimension kind of commute.

And yes, if MMM is commutative, then BMBMBM is monoidal, although the axioms are the only nontrivial part of the monoidal product. The [[Day convolution]] on this monoidal product would be ... yeah, I think it actually is that product when you work out which coequalizer computes the coend.

It's pretty late for me too, but if/when comonoids for Day convolution are comonadic, and when the comonad is left exact, you get a [[geometric surjection]] and therefore a topos. I don't know what the conditions on a monoidal category are to get comonadicity of comonoids on the presheaf category with Day convolution though.

Under the assumption that MMM is a monoid, equipped with an homomorphism ℓ:M→(N,+)\ell : M \to (\mathbb N,+)ℓ:M→(N,+) such that ℓ(m)=0\ell(m)=0ℓ(m)=0 if and only if mmm is a unit in MMM, one can prove that a counital comagma in SetM{\bf Set}^MSetM is automatically coassociative and cocommutative, because

  1. Every counital comagma (S,α)(S,\alpha)(S,α) is an object of the full subcategory D⊆SetM\mathcal D \subseteq {\bf Set}^MD⊆SetM with the property that, for every s∈Ss\in Ss∈S there exists aaa such that s=α(s).as = \alpha(s) . as=α(s).a (the dot is the monoid action);
  2. Restricted on D\mathcal DD, which is a monoidal subcategory, Day convolution coincides with Cartesian product.

Then, by Fox theorem, every object is a cocommutative comonoid and every morphism a coalgebra homomorphism for this structure.

Clearly ℓ\ellℓ is the identity function, for MMM the monoid of natural numbers. One can prove the above statement in general, but for natural numbers the category of N\mathbb NN-sets acquires the particuarly explicit shape of the category of sets (X,t)(X,t)(X,t) equipped with an endofunction t:X→Xt : X \to Xt:X→X (+its iterates). In that case, the property that a counital comagma ((X,t),ϵ)((X,t),\epsilon)((X,t),ϵ) satisfies via its counit ϵ:X→N\epsilon : X \to \mathbb Nϵ:X→N is that

Every x∈Xx\in Xx∈X with ϵ(x)=n\epsilon(x)=nϵ(x)=n has the form x=tnzx=t^n zx=tnz for some zzz with ϵ(z)=0\epsilon(z)=0ϵ(z)=0

Okay, so my remark on uniqueness of comonoid structures in cartesian categories was not completely useless, just missing the point in a major way.
